items.note: Story 1 gives the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891.
Article VII quoted verbatim: paid by pounds of butterfat ascertained by test, not by weight of milk, and the test of the station where he delivers governs.
Story 1 states the rule made one station's own test equipment, with no cross-check, the entire basis of every patron's pay - the sentence the whole trouble turned on.

Of the three officers only Hobart Sill appears in Section A, and only in passing as a source and lender of glassware; Effie Loomis absent, Wilbur Teague named only in Section C, which cannot travel into A.

Selby Vose appears nowhere in Section A; the son/manager-from-1913 material would have to come from B3/B4, and B-G credit never travels into Section A. (The run also dates him to 1911, which is a planted error.)
The station-gain ledger line is stated only at C1(a); nothing about it in Section A.
Story 2: Ostrey Hollow, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, opened with glassware lent from Larrow Green.

Section A gives only 'weighed, tested, and separated on the spot; cream hauled down, skim home'. No composite sample, no fixed charge from the pipette, no percent read on the graduated neck (that mechanism appears only at C1(a), in Section C).
Outfit ordered from Ammon & Sons on the invoice of 14 April 1897 and in use from 1 May 1897, with the 1898 and 1899 rivals named and rejected.
Invoice itemized: six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, summing to $77.93; the $77.39 variant is attributed, not asserted.
The flat, every-month 0.19 shortfall is stated at C1(b), inside Section C; nothing on the shortfall's flatness appears in Section A.

Nothing anywhere about a pipette being uncheckable without a burette, or that no burette existed in the county; the run affirmatively claims at C1(a) that no calibration figure for the pipette exists.

Story 2: Ansel Keddie tester and separator man from the day the station opened (4 May 1896), twenty-nine seasons without a break, ending 1925. Service and its end carried; the exact 30 April dismissal date is missing but the item's own aspect is the service and its end.
No mention of the test book, its columns, or the bench routine anywhere in Section A.
The summary leaf and its 3.80 / 3.61 pair appear only in Section C.
The nine weeks of 1911 - broken pipette 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, 3.80 through the interval, the question mark - is entirely absent.
Section A says only that Orra Keddie's 'own family' were 'the Brants'. It never states she was Emmet Brant's sister; at B2 the run expressly says that identification is nowhere stated.
The 1919 circular's content and Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement are absent from Section A; Story 3 only says the matter 'stayed closed... until 1919 - a later story'.
No death in 1934, no impounding of the test book, no county historical rooms.
Answers 'granddaughter'.

Grounds it on the report's own appended closing correction ('the granddaughter and not the great-niece; the error on page two is mine') - one of the two resolutions the key names, and the great-niece claim is rejected rather than absorbed. The Duncan-Keddie generation chain is not spelled out.

Second cousins, with the full derivation worked out (Hazel = Emmet's granddaughter via Roy; Duncan = Emmet's sister's son and Roy's first cousin; Ivy = Ansel's granddaughter), and the open premise flagged as the question asks.

Abstention item A08 not addressed at all: the run never raises whether Emmet and Orra were full or half siblings, so it neither declines it nor notes that it does not change the answer. No assertion either, so no gullibility deduction.
Gideon Vose, his father; the 'nephew' version identified as a circulating error and rejected with named sources.

Borderline but credited under the B-G scope rule: at B4 the run states that Gideon wrote the by-law making a station's own test the basis of every patron's pay and that his son signed the 1919 circular accusing those same patrons. B3's own stated significance (inherited unquestioned authority) is not the key's.

Correct abstention on A01: the headline is 'None that the sources establish by blood or marriage', an evidence claim rather than a verdict, and the passage says plainly that any tie 'cannot be determined from the sources - ... silence isn't proof of absence'.

What is established is got wrong: the run says 'none is claimed anywhere', where the key's establishable content is that two narrators assert a cousinship from talk, one denies it flatly, no document names or denies a link, and a family member's denial is not a record.

Answer matches the key: the tests read 95 percent of true, short by exactly 5 percent. Working is weak - it back-derives 0.19/3.80 and wrongly claims the sources give no calibration figure for the pipette, so the 16.72 vs 17.6 route the question asks for is missed - but the proportion itself is the keyed value.
True average 3.80, recorded tests short by 0.19 of a point.
76,000 lb, from 40,000,000 x 0.0019, with the 25-year window justified; the 67,000 lb rival is attributed to the 1925 petition, not adopted.
$19,000 and 20 percent / one fifth, both required elements. $19,600 is discussed and expressly rejected, so it is not absorbed.
Declined outright: the run says the largest patron cannot be identified and no 1910 individual figure exists. C2 is not an abstention item; 6,840 lb is required.
Declined; 360 lb not given.
Declined; $86.40 not given.

deductions.reason: Corruption: asserts Selby Vose became manager in 1911 (B3, repeated at B4) as fact; the canonical year is 1913 and 1911 is a catalogued planted error.
